overview.body:
**Iphigeneia** ​(*iphigeneia*) — ‌Sacrifice, ‌Winds, ​Aulis · ​Mighty-born ​(ἶφι "by ​might" ​+ γένος ‌"birth") ​— ​belongs to ‌the ​Greek tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued ​under ​the domain ​"Sacrifice, ​Winds, Aulis". ​The ‌name ​means "Mighty-born ‌(ἶφι ​"by might" ‌+ ​γένος "birth")".

‌**Iphigeneia** ​is ‌sacrifice, winds, ​aulis. ​The name ‌means ‌"Mighty-born (ἶφι ‌"by ​might" ​+ γένος ‌"birth")" ​and belongs ​to ‌the ​greek tradition.

​PuniCodex ‌restores the ​name ‌as **Iphigeneia** ​and ​serves ​its temple ​at ‌[its temple](https://punicodex.com/iphigeneia/). ‌The ​original ‌preserves one ​prosodic ​feature — ‌stress ‌or vowel ‌length ‌— ​rather than ‌both, ​which places ​the ​name in ‌Tier ​2. ​The plain ​ASCII ‌form *iphigeneia* ​survives ​as ​a modern ‌convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system; ​the ‌restoration, not ‌the ​fallback, is ​the ​form the ​project ‌defends ‌as philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Greek ​as **Ἰφιγένεια**. ​Etymologically it ​means "Mighty-born ​(ἶφι ​"by might" ‌+ γένος ​"birth")".

​The ASCII ‌form *iphigeneia* ​survives only ‌because ​the early ‌domain-name system ​could ​not carry ​diacritics; it ​is ​a technological ‌compromise, not ​an ancient ‌spelling. ​The Unicode ‌restoration **Iphigeneia** ​recovers ‌the full ​diacritic detail ‌of ​the scholarly ​transliteration directly ‌in the ‌address ‌bar. The ​original preserves ​one ‌prosodic feature ​— stress ​or vowel ‌length ​— rather ​than both, ‌which ​places the ‌name in ​Tier ​2.

The ​letter-by-letter transformation ​runs:

- ‌**i** ‌→ **I** ​— Smooth ‌breathing
​- **p** ​→ **p** ‌— Pi
‌- ‌**h** → ‌**h** — ​Aspiration ‌of phi
​- **i** ​→ ​**i** — ‌Iota
- ​**g** → ​**g** ​— Gamma
‌- **e** ​→ ​**e** — ​Epsilon
- ‌**n** ​→ **n** ‌— Nu
​- **e** ‌→ ​**e** — ‌Diphthong ei
‌- ​**i** → ​**i** — ​Diphthong ei
​- ‌**a** → ‌**a** — ​Alpha

pronunciation.body:

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**iphigeneia** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Iphigeneia.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"iphigeneia" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Iphigeneia".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"iphigeneia" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Iphigeneia" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Iphigeneia was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Iphigeneia ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Iphigeneia ‌place sacrifice, ​winds, ​aulis ​at the ​center ​of a ‌living ​mythological world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Iphigeneia ‌appears ​in greek ‌tradition ​as sacrifice, ​winds, ​aulis. The ​name's ​meaning, "Mighty-born ‌(ἶφι ​"by ‌might" + ​γένος ‌"birth")", shapes ​the ‌narratives told ​about ‌this figure.

​### ​Worship ‌and Memory ‌(Cult)

‌Devotees and ​later ​tradition-keepers preserved ‌Iphigeneia ​in ritual, ​text, ‌and ​iconography, ensuring ​the ‌name survived ​into ‌the modern ​scholarly ​record.

​The myths ​of ‌Iphigeneia survive ‌in ​fragments, summaries, ‌and ​later retellings. ​Each ‌version ‌reflects the ‌interests ‌of its ​tellers ‌— poets, ​priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ‌The ​PuniCodex entry ​does ​not privilege ‌a ​single version; ​it ​gathers the ‌attestations ​so ‌that readers ​can ‌compare them. ​The ‌restoration Iphigeneia ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable ​name around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Iphigeneia ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Greek ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Ἰφιγένεια, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​sacrifice ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Iphigeneia is ‌to ​hold ​the idea ​of ​sacrifice, ​Winds, Aulis ‌in ​the ​mind and ‌to ​ask ‌what of ​it ‌endures. ​The name ​means ​"Mighty-born ​(ἶφι "by ​might" ‌+ ​γένος "birth")" ‌— ​and ‌a name ​that ‌carries ​its meaning ‌so ​openly ​invites meditation ‌rather ‌than ‌mere recollection. ​The ​tradition ‌remembers the ​name ​as ‌sacrifice, Winds, ​Aulis ​· ‌Mighty-born (ἶφι ​"by ‌might" ​+ γένος ​"birth").

​Sit ​with the ‌restored ‌form ​— Iphigeneia ‌— ​and ​the diacritics ‌themselves ‌become ‌the practice: ‌each ​mark ‌is a ​small ​act ​of attention, ‌a ​refusal ​to let ​the ‌plain ​ASCII form ​*iphigeneia* ​stand ‌in for ​the ‌whole. ​What the ‌tradition ​preserved ‌in this ‌name, ​the ​restoration asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
